subject: Follow-up: model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps:

- Goal: add a latent-search powered "assistant" in Acme’s storefront to help shoppers with sizing and product-fit questions.
- Key success metrics you shared: conversion delta vs baseline, and a 95th percentile latency target of <200ms for interactive flows.
- Traffic profile: expected steady-state ~300 TPS with spikes up to ~800 TPS during peak.
- Data: you mentioned a small sample of anonymized customer queries and product catalog excerpts — that would be ideal for a quick model-fit eval.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Share sample payloads (JSON) and a short list of "golden" prompts / success cases — you can attach or drop a Drive link.
2) We'll run a Redwood model-fit eval against 2-3 candidate models and return a short report (latency percentiles, TPS, qualitative error modes) + prompt set suggestions.
3) Quick sync next week to review findings and recommend a pilot configuration (model variant, quantization, batching).

Marissa (cc) will include our benchmark links and a Redwood-verified performance profile for the candidate models — that should help set expectations for latency/TPS tradeoffs.

Thanks again — if you can send the sample payloads (or point me to an S3/Drive link) and confirm whether the 95th <200ms target is a hard requirement, we’ll prioritize accordingly.

Best,
Alex
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

- Attached is a small sample (anonymized) of ~1k queries and product snippets for an initial eval (see attachment: acme_sample_payloads.json).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmeretail.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood-verified performance profiles + recommended models

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Quick summary from our pre-run review and historical profiles for similar storefront QA workloads. High-level recommendations below; I’ve attached the more detailed CSV + PDF.

Recommended candidates (initial):
- rwf-7B-v2 (8-bit quant): best latency/quality balance for short Q&A; typical 95th ~ 140–180ms at 300 TPS with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled.
- redwood-mini-13B-quant (gptq-8): higher quality on long-form product reasoning; 95th ~ 250–320ms at 300 TPS (depends on prompt length) — may need a higher-cost tier or aggressive quantization/batching to meet 200ms target.

Redwood-verified sample numbers (expected range, full runs attached):
- rwf-7B-v2: TPS sustainable: 320–380; 50/90/95/99 latencies: 45/95/165/310 ms
- redwood-mini-13B-quant: TPS sustainable: 180–250; 50/90/95/99 latencies: 80/160/270/520 ms

Notes on quality regressions and guardrails:
- Down-quantizing (gptq-8) can introduce hallucination risk on long-context prompts — we recommend a focused eval on your "golden" prompts to detect regression.
- We suggest a small human-labeled eval set (50–100 cases) to verify semantic fidelity before a production rollout.
- If 95th <200ms is a hard SLA, rwf-7B-v2 looks like the safer initial choice; we can run a quality-focused pass to ensure it meets your accuracy bar.

Attachments: prompt_sets_v1.zip, benchmark_summary.csv, redwood_performance_profiles.pdf

Next steps:
1) Alex to confirm we have the final sample set (Sarah).
2) Dylan to run the baseline runs and upload raw traces.
3) We'll deliver a one-page recommendation + a short recording reviewing trade-offs — target: Thursday EOD.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the profiles — Thu 2pm PT open for us.

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acmeretail.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood-verified performance profiles + recommended models

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple questions:

1) The latency numbers for rwf-7B-v2 look promising — can you share the exact run config (sequence length, batching window, KV-cache settings) used to produce the 95th 165ms number?
2) For the redwood-mini-13B-quant, is there a recommended hybrid approach (e.g., route short queries to 7B, long-form product reasoning to 13B) and how hard is that to operate?

We’d like Redwood to run the eval on our sample and surface any quality regressions against our golden prompts. If you can run the baseline and drop the raw traces, we’ll arrange a 30-min review on Thu 2pm PT.

One more ask — do you have a short write-up on how you test for regression post-quantization? We need that for our internal compliance review.

Best,
Sarah
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood-verified performance profiles + recommended models

Hi all —

I can own the baseline run. Plan:
- Run both candidates (rwf-7B-v2 @ gptq-8 and redwood-mini-13B-quant) on Acme sample set with the following config: max_seq=512, batching window=20ms, continuous KV cache enabled for prefix reuse.
- Produce per-request traces (latency + token counts), aggregated percentiles, and an MRR/accuracy pass against your golden prompts.
- Run a small quantization regression test: label 100 random cases from the sample and compare outputs between fp16 and gptq-8 variants to flag semantic drift.

Timeline: I’ll start today and aim to post raw traces + benchmark_summary.csv to the Drive folder within 48 hours. If you can share an S3 or Drive link to the full sample (or confirm the attached file is the complete set), I’ll queue the jobs.

Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/model-fit-eval (read-only)

Thanks —
Dylan
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
